business_summary.text: Max Estates develops residential and commercial real estate in Delhi NCR, with operational office assets (Max Towers, Max House, Max Square) and a residential launch pipeline.

call_points.text: Net debt ₹234 Cr at June 2026; gross debt ₹1,960 Cr including ₹934 Cr of lease rental discounting, cash ₹1,727 Cr.
₹1,500–1,800 Cr of commercial capex remains, fully tied up; construction finance converts to lease rental discounting on completion.
Pre-leasing pipeline in excess of 3 million sq ft under discussion across the two under-construction commercial projects.
Elevated employee and marketing costs reflect launches this quarter versus none a year ago; costs to track launches through the year.
Residential sales volumes moderated through the quarter on global uncertainty, tightening liquidity and cautious consumer sentiment.
No FY27 pre-sales guidance; management cited an evolving macro situation and declined even a directional range.
About ₹17,000 Cr of GDV is yet to come to market, to be launched in phases.
FY26 operating cash flow was ₹450–500 Cr; management said it is bullish on OCF in coming years.
About ₹1,200 Cr surplus sits in RERA accounts, enough for residential construction; no project debt foreseen.
Q4 rental income rose partly on an Ind AS rental equalisation adjustment, not only escalations.
Management said inflation has so far been absorbed through escalation and contingency budgets, but prolonged geopolitical strain could hurt.
Residential demand is cautious across ticket sizes; management sees end-user demand but slower decision-making.

exceptions: fine or penalty ₹5.64 lakh: Joint Commissioner-II, Municipal Corporation, Manesar (Notice received for Max Estates Gurgaon Two Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company) under Section 122 of Hary)

penalties.details: Notice received for Max Estates Gurgaon Two Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company) under Section 122 of Haryana Municipal Corporation Act, 1991 read with Haryana Municipal Corporation Advertisement Bye-Laws, 2022 imposing penalty of ₹5,64,399/- for displaying advertisement, in contravention of Section 122 of Haryana Municipal Corporation Act, 1991
penalties.impact: Financial impact is limited to ₹5,64,399/- towards penalty; there is no impact on operations. The Subsidiary has submitted its response to the notice and is taking appropriate steps for resolution of the matter.

penalties.authority: Additional/Joint Director of Income Tax (Intelligence & Criminal Investigation), New Delhi, Income Tax Department, Government of India
penalties.details: Order under Section 271FAA imposing penalty of Rs 50,000 for inaccurate/incomplete filing of Statement of Financial Transaction (Form 61A) for FY 2024-25 in the case of Max Estates Gurgaon Two Limited (wholly owned subsidiary of the Company)
penalties.impact: Financial impact limited to penalty of Rs 50,000; no impact on operations. Given the small quantum, the impact is not material at the consolidated level. The Subsidiary will file the appeal to Commissioner of Income-Tax (Appeals) as the error is due to technical glitch on tax Portal

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Pharmax Corporation Limited, a subsidiary of Max Estates Limited, received a Show Cause Notice in Form GST DRC-01 dated July 27, 2026, under Section 73 of the CGST/DGST Acts for FY 2022-23, proposing demand of Rs 5.90 Crores (including tax, interest and penalty), relating to alleged excess / ineligible input tax credit. The matter was at the show cause notice stage, with no final demand or order passed.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Department of Trade and Taxes, Government of NCT of Delhi (Office of the Assistant Commissioner / GSTO)
tax_litigation.status: The Company has opposed the proposed demand, considering it factually incorrect and without merit, as the major amounts of Input Tax Credit (ITC) identified by the Department had already been reversed in the Company's books and GST returns. The proposed demand appears to have arisen from an automated reconciliation of vendors' outward supplies, GSTR-2B and GSTR-9 disclosures, without considering the ITC reversals already undertaken by the Company. The matter is currently pending adjudication. The reply to the Show Cause Notice has been submitted, and the date of personal hearing is awaited.

guidance.statement: FY27 collections expected at ₹2,500–3,000 Cr, with project deployment of ₹1,500–1,800 Cr
Targets adding about 2 million sq ft residential and 1 million sq ft commercial development annually
guidance.target: 2 mn sq ft residential and 1 mn sq ft commercial per year

guidance.statement: Project deployment of ₹1,500–1,800 Cr in FY27, leaving OCF of ₹750–1,000 Cr for business development
Annual rental income of about ₹700 Cr at peak occupancy from current and under-construction assets
Target annual addition of 2 million sq ft of residential development
Target 1 million sq ft of new commercial business development a year, over and above the ₹700 Cr annuity
No FY27 pre-sales guidance will be given

industry: Consumer Discretionary > Realty > Residential, Commercial Projects

operating_notes.text: FY26 average residential realisation was ₹23,000 per sq ft, up from ₹18,000 in FY24.
Operational commercial assets total 1.2 million sq ft at 100% occupancy, generating ₹150 Cr lease rental income in FY26.
Unrecognised revenue from launch projects is ₹16,310 Cr, of which ₹12,500 Cr is sold and contracted, with embedded PBT estimated at ₹4,200–4,900 Cr.

Total revenue potential across launched residential and mixed-use portfolio is ₹17,500 Cr, of which ₹13,500 Cr is sold and contracted (₹3,500 Cr collected, ₹10,000 Cr to be collected), with embedded PBT of ₹4,500–5,500 Cr.
Residential launch pipeline is about ₹16,100 Cr: ₹4,000 Cr launched and available this year and about ₹12,000 Cr of new launches planned through FY27.
Commercial assets Max Towers, Max House and Max Square are 100% leased across 1.2 million sq ft, with Max Towers' latest lease at ₹156 per sq ft per month against a ₹132 weighted average.

timeline.summary: On 26 May 2026 Max Estates told its Q4FY26 call that FY26 pre-sales were ₹5,305 Cr, collections ₹1,578 Cr and net debt about ₹100 Cr, and declined to guide FY27 pre-sales.

On 17 August 2026 Max Estates' Q1FY27 call reported pre-sales of about ₹1,100 Cr (5x YoY) and collections of ₹575 Cr, and ICRA assigned a first-time A+ (stable) issuer rating covering the company and 14 subsidiaries.
